notes: The original. A megalodon's body — available from the first boss of every run.
Faster and turns harder than the shark. Held back to level 15 so it reads as an escalation.

The kraken. The one boss that does not come to you: it holds mid-range, circles, and fills the water with ink you cannot see through — see systems/kraken.js. Held to level 20 because it is the hardest arrival to READ, and a player meeting it as their first boss would have no idea what the ink was for. sizeMul is under the other two animals' on purpose — much of this body's length is arm, which carries no hitbox. ownNames is left FALSE: it takes the general pool plus the parts tagged for it.

The king crab. The one boss that walks: it holds the seabed and hauls itself off it at you, so the fight is fought in the layer the chum settles in — see CONFIG.enemies.bossCrab. sizeMul is the highest in the file and that is a fact about the BODY, not an escalation: a crab's radius describes its half-height (it doubles as how high it rests off the sand) while its silhouette is three times as wide, so the same on-screen size as a shark costs a much bigger multiplier. Held to level 12 so it is never a run's first boss — every archetype after the first arrives with a perk, and a floor-bound boss wants the reach one of those buys it. ownNames TRUE: a crab is not a fish and should not roll the pool's swimming words.

The mosasaur. The fifth swimming archetype and the only one that is not a shark, an orca or a squid — see enemyMosasaur in assets.js for why that silhouette was worth a slot. Fights like the shark does, on purpose: it chases, and the counterplay is its turning circle, which is the widest in the file (1.15 against the kraken's 1.7). What it has instead of a bespoke system is the only authored BITE besides the megalodon's — 62 degrees of gape over 1.68s — so its one committed attack is a thing the player watches happen rather than a number applied to them. sizeMul 1.6 makes it the longest final body in the game at 27.2 units, which is the whole claim this animal makes. Held to level 10 so it is never a run's first boss: it hits harder than the shark and reads the same way, so meeting it first would just be a harder shark.

The trawler that shoots back. Rides the surface and shells the water — see systems/bossBoat.js. Held to level 10 so it is never a run's first boss: it is the one fight that is not about swimming at something.
